title: p11scope/inventory/v1 object_observations section (H9, version 7)
description: Consumer contract for H9 section version 7: identical to version 6 except the section version constant (7) and the inferred_family/inferred_size keys on every proved key row (inferred-from-mechanism family both modes, inferred-from-length size under --key-sizes; unknown/conflicting/unsupported statuses with first-two-pinned conflicts, completions counting evidence-carrying terminals, reasons in -v text only). Version 7 is emitted exactly when a row carries non-blank inferred content; versions 1-6 stay frozen and byte-stable. Older text: version 6 was identical to version 5 except the section version constant (6), the per-field source key on every metadata field (query, creation_success or null), the per-field reason key naming truncation, unsupported values, unusable curves and partly-read templates, the sixteen new-site metadata_labels (x25519/x448/ed25519/ed448, hkdf_96/128/192/256/384/other, generic_96/128/192/256/384/other), the CKK_HKDF key-type code (66) in metadata_field_key_type, the 12/48 sizes in metadata_field_value_len, and the four curve names in metadata_field_curve. Version 6 is emitted exactly when new-site content is present (a new-site label, the HKDF key-type scalar, a 12/48 value length, a new curve name, an established field with a non-`query` source, a view created from a truncated template, or an unsupported-value, unusable-curve or partly-read reason). Versions 1-5 stay frozen; consumers dispatch on the section version and refuse unknown versions. Frozen consumer contract for the H9 operation/key delivery and presentation section of p11scope/inventory/v1 documents (Task 4, H9 section 3). Every object is closed: additionalProperties is false at every level, and every enum is exact. Consumers (JSON readers, JSONL reconstructors, the dashboard) must read only this contract, never reducer internals or friendly labels. Row counters are cumulative within their row: repeated cumulative JSONL snapshots (kinds object_observed and key_operations_observed) replace rows by (bucket, row key, revision) and must never be summed as deltas. A row is keyed by its full key tuple; a greater revision replaces an older one; rows never delete (retained history is immutable). A row event's revision is its last change: the emitter sends only changed rows per revision, so unchanged rows persist client-side below the pass marker's object_revision. status names object authority, not S1 health: unavailable/partial/stale never imply S1 loss. Unknown-key summaries never carry started (starts are never fabricated into the unknown bucket). No raw handles, pointers, native keys, epochs, PIDs/TIDs, address-derived hashes or arbitrary attribute bytes appear anywhere in this section.

version.description: Section version. Additive versioned section; consumers must reject unknown versions, never guess.

revision.description: Publication revision (production: coordinator passes at capture). JSONL rows carry their revision; greater replaces older.

status.description: populated: complete authority. partial: row/budget refusal omitted associations (S1 preserved). stale: retained older complete publication; the newer revision could not publish, and old active rows are historical, not current authority. unavailable: no Joint object evidence (S1 unaffected).

reason.description: Finite machine reason. none only when status is populated. journal_unavailable names the v0.5.0 world (no journal producer linked, so no key-operation feed exists); bootstrap_unavailable keeps its 0.6.0 meaning (journal linked, no birth yet); live_joint_feed_absent names retained folded-Joint evidence with no live Joint feed (partial, never unavailable). serialization_refused is reserved: the JSON encoder is infallible, so current producers never emit it.

sessions.description: Model sessions, sorted by session id. Snapshot-only: the JSONL stream carries session lifecycle through object_observed rows, not a session kind.

objects.description: Object views, sorted by object id. Counters are successful references, never distinct keys, completed operations or physical token inventory.

key_operations.description: Proved-key aggregate rows, sorted by (instance, object, category, role, metadata_at_use). Role rows count associations and cannot be summed across roles into a global operation denominator.

unknown_key_operations.description: Capture-wide unknown-key summaries, sorted by (category, reason). Terminals partition here once per primary operation role; started is never present, never fabricated.

unattributed.description: Not-attributed counters in frozen reason order, zero reasons omitted: calls that carry no per-key row, with the finite reason no key could be proved (started_before_attach counts direct reductions on a feed registered without a witnessed birth). Counts and reason names only; attributed rows beside them stay exact.

occupied.description: Unknown summaries are finite by construction (category x reason, capture-wide): no limit, no refusal path.

encoded_bytes.description: Measured JSON encoding bytes of this section at commit. A measurement, never an RSS estimate or heap-bound proof.

allocation_refused.description: Byte-pool refusal. No pool is frozen (owner gate): always false until a reviewed pool ships with a schema update.

refusal_reason.description: Pool refusal reason. Always none until a reviewed pool ships.

session.description: Public capture-local session id (monotonic model id, not a raw handle).

value.description: Retained CKA_CLASS code (0 data, 1 certificate, 2 public_key, 3 private_key, 4 secret_key). Public JSON carries the accepted numeric code; labels are presentation names. Never key material.

source.description: How this field was established: a provider attribute-result read (query) or a successful creation return promoting its own finite template (creation_success). An established value always carries query or creation_success; requested blocks and every non-value status carry null.

enum: template value outside approved finite set
reason.description: Why a field stays unknown — or, for a mismatched Edwards/Montgomery curve, why its key type stays unlabeled: the truncation reason for fields never seen on a truncated template, the unsupported reason for kinds seen with an unclassifiable value (a value outside the approved finite set, or an unavailable, malformed or size-only cell), the curve reason for a mismatched Edwards/Montgomery curve on a created object whose own template was seen, or (on a complete C_CreateObject or public-half C_GenerateKeyPair template) an unestablished one, the partly-read reason for fields never seen on a partly-read template. Null for every other field.

value.description: Retained CKA_KEY_TYPE code at OASIS numbers (0 rsa, 1 dsa, 2 dh, 3 ec, 4 x9_42_dh, 16 generic_secret, 31 aes, 64 ec_edwards, 65 ec_montgomery, 66 hkdf, 73 ml_kem, 74 ml_dsa, 75 slh_dsa). Public JSON carries the accepted numeric code; labels are presentation names. Never key material.

metadata_label.description: Frozen label from established facts: RSA modulus bits, AES/HKDF/generic-secret value length in bits, finite curve. Established facts come from observed attribute results and, since v6, from complete finite creation templates honored by a successful return (requested CKA_TOKEN, unknown/conflict shapes and incomplete triples still never label). One provenance exception: an RSA private key from C_GenerateKeyPair carries its pair-mate public key's established size when both handles came from the same successful return; its own established.modulus_bits stays unknown. The additional version-4 label 'unknown' names a first-observed key whose identity and counts are proved but whose type/size were never established in the observed window; it is never a guessed type or size. The eighteen version-5 labels name a PQC parameter set joined with its established key type (ML-DSA-44/65/87, ML-KEM-512/768/1024, the twelve SLH-DSA hash/size/function sets); anything else (missing type, missing set, out-of-range code, conflict, incompatible class) labels nothing and the use partitions metadata_unknown/metadata_conflicting. The sixteen version-6 labels name a Montgomery/Edwards curve (x25519/x448/ed25519/ed448) or an HKDF/generic-secret byte size in bits (96/128/192/256/384, plus an unreachable _other each); like every label, each needs its established key type and size/curve.

gap_reason.description: Model gap vocabulary (snake_case of the finite model enum) plus pruned_object_referenced: a retained key row references an object the model pruned (history stays; the dangle is explicit, never silent). v7 adds corroboration_mismatch: the corroborating length disagreed with the terminal length (the terminal still classifies; v1-v6 never carry it). v7 also adds wrapped_park_refused: a wrapped-material park was refused past the park budget (inference-side; rows intact, coverage populated; v1-v6 never carry it).

object.description: Public capture-local object id (monotonic model id, not a raw handle).

birth.description: Observed call interval, never physical age. Null when unknown.

lifetime_reason.description: Reason for access_ended/retired; null for live/destroyed.

attribution_reason.description: Reason for downgraded; null while valid.

unit.description: operations for ordinary categories; message_contexts for message_* categories. Never signatures-per-message.

instance.description: Existing registry instance id label (joinable to instances[]).

unknown.description: The S1 unknown terminal while the key relationship stayed proven; not an S1-outcome change.

key_join_lost.description: Ends only the key association; not an S1 outcome. Row equation: started = completed + failed + cancelled + unknown + active + key_join_lost (before counter saturation).

status.description: inferred: one family. unknown: no evidence or evidence outside every map (named reason in -v text only). conflicting: two distinct values, or an incompatible established fact (established side omitted: the label stands on the row). unsupported: never reported for families.

value.description: First-seen family, or null when unknown. The secret superclass never conflicts.

completions.description: Completions carrying family evidence (mechanism present) behind this row, not only the valued ones.

conflict_value.description: Second distinct inferred family (omitted unless two inferred values observed; the secret superclass never appears here).

conflict_completions.description: Completions behind the conflict value (omitted with it).

further_conflicts.description: Further distinct values counted, never listed (omitted when 0; first two stay pinned).

status.description: inferred: one size. unknown: no evidence or evidence outside every map (named reason in -v text only). conflicting: two distinct sizes, or a contradicting established size. unsupported: evidence exists but the subset has no map, or the length is outside the subset admission bound (RSA outside 64..=2048, AES-KW material above 8191; the refused completion still counts, JSON unsupported sets only from a weak unknown, -v prints size unsupported (outside admission bound) only when that reason is set; publishes no size, parks nothing; never overwrites inferred, never flips).

detail.description: First-seen size detail, or null when unknown/unsupported. Same size means same kind plus size params; the evidence tag does not count.

completions.description: Completions carrying attached length evidence behind this row: valued or unavailable observations count while the flag is on, and a direct observation still counts when size classification refuses it.

conflict_detail.description: Second distinct size detail, same shape as detail (omitted unless two inferred sizes observed).

further_conflicts.description: Further distinct sizes counted, never listed (omitted when 0; first two stay pinned).

kind.description: Size kind. rsa carries size_class plus modulus_bytes; rsa_nonstandard carries modulus_bytes only (masked class in text, never a range); ec/eddsa carry curve plus octets; dsa_class carries the pinned legacy label; pqc_set carries the parameter set; wrapped_material sizes the wrapped key, never the wrapping key.

evidence.description: The length evidence kind behind this detail (first tag kept on same-size repeats).

size_class.description: Standard RSA size (1024/2048/3072/4096); absent for non-standard octets.

curve.description: EC raw-field curve or EdDSA curve.

octets.description: Classified signature/ciphertext/output octets, or the wrap/unwrap length for wrapped material.

label.description: Pinned DSA legacy class (ambiguous classes said so).

parameter_set.description: PQC parameter set (SHA2-vs-SHAKE stays ambiguous for shared SLH-DSA sizes).

material_octets.description: Wrapped-key material octets (L-8 for plain AES-KW wrap output and fresh-view unwrap input, admitted 0..=8191 with L 8..=8199; on a proved wrapped-key row a larger observed value contributes no new size but counts its completion: the row JSON status reads unsupported only when its prior size state is a weak unknown (the above-bound direct completion sets it), -v prints size unsupported (outside admission bound) only when that reason is set, and prior inferred, conflicting or stronger unknown state stays; on a rowless wrap or fresh-view unwrap it leaves no park and contributes no wrapped-size evidence to the subsequent row).

about.description: Wrapped material is always about the wrapped key.

unknown_reason.description: unbound: no receipt at start. key_join_lost: retirement ended a known association before the terminal. metadata_unknown/conflicting: known object, unusable label at use. role_unavailable: KEM (no approved object role). not_applicable: generation and ordinary digest (existing S1 units).
